name: Worst Mistakes
definition: For a nonempty binary class $\mathcal H$ on a finite domain $X$, fix a permutation $\pi$ of all of $X$, known to the learner before play. At each coordinate the deterministic learner predicts a label and receives the true label of an unknown fixed target $h\in\mathcal H$. It must predict every coordinate once. Let $b(\mathcal H,\pi)$ be the minimum over learners of the maximum number of mistakes over targets. The **Worst Mistakes** parameter is $\max_{\pi}b(\mathcal H,\pi)$. The empty domain has value zero.
graph_summary: Mistake bound when an adversary chooses the presentation sequence and the learner may be transductive.
origin_references: The adversarially ordered (worst) and favorably ordered mistake models are studied in \cite{ben1997online}.

monotonic.proof: A prediction strategy whose adversarial mistake bound holds for every target in $\mathcal H$ has the same bound when the target is known to lie in a subfamily $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$.

c_monotonic.proof: A mistake-bound learner for the original class restricts to a conditioned fibre by answering fixed-coordinate predictions for free; its mistake bound cannot increase.

p_monotonic.proof: Let $\mathcal R=\mathcal H|_T$. Fix a representative in $\mathcal H$ for every target trace in $\mathcal R$. Any adversarial presentation sequence on $T$ with labels from such a trace is also a valid presentation sequence for its representative in $\mathcal H$. Restricting an optimal worst-case predictor for $\mathcal H$ to those sequences therefore gives the same bound for $\mathcal R$.

doubly_monotonic.proof: This is the conjunction of the established subfamily- and projection-monotonicity arguments.
